{"judgments": [
 {"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"The insuring promise turns on 'due proof' and on the insured dying 'while the contract was in force', both of which are open-textured and here badly garbled.","reasoning_cat2":"It is expressly 'subject to its terms', so it must be read with the Grace Period (c023), Suicide (c034) and Incontestability (c033) provisions that cut back the promise; that interaction is a plausible but not obvious source of conflict.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
 {"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"A 20-day free-look right whose text is fragmentary ('within those 20 days ... refund the premiums that were paid to us') leaves the trigger and mechanics uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits directly against the state-specific Notice to Policyholder return rights (c003-c006), which give 30 or 45 days for replacement policies, so which period governs a replacement policy is a genuine question.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.38},
 {"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"This is only a caption listing states with the operative sentence missing, so nothing in it can be applied as written.","reasoning_cat2":"It is one of a set of overlapping free-look provisions (c002, c004, c005, c006) whose combined effect on a replacement policy is not spelled out.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.29},
 {"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"The clause hinges on whether the policy 'replaces an existing policy', an undefined term, and the text is transposed and truncated.","reasoning_cat2":"It gives 30 days where the policy face gives 20 (c002) and PA gets 45 (c006), an unresolved overlap in a case about a replacement policy.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.36},
 {"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"The California version repeats the 'replaces an existing policy' trigger and is missing words ('FOR AN [UNCONDITIONAL FULL REFUND OF]').","reasoning_cat2":"It is a state carve-out from the general 20-day right (c002) and duplicates c004's 30-day rule, but as a CA-only term it is unlikely to bear on this policy.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.22},
 {"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"The PA paragraph is the most mangled of the set, with the operative period ('within 45 days of delivery if we issue your ... policy') detached from any subject.","reasoning_cat2":"For a policy litigated in a Pennsylvania federal court this is the state term that would displace the 20-day right in c002, so the relationship is squarely in play.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.35},
 {"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"A boilerplate footnote whose lines are out of order, but its message - premiums depend on risk class and no one may promise a change - is clear enough.","reasoning_cat2":"It is consistent with the Risk Class definition (c021) and the renewal premium table (c014); no conflict appears.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
 {"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"Identical footnote on the rider specification page; scrambled but substantively determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates c007 and c014 without contradicting them or the Accelerated Benefit Rider terms.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.06},
 {"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"A single mechanical statement that installments are monthly per $1,000 of proceeds; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"It matches the option descriptions (c038-c046) and the actuarial basis note (c013).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.04},
 {"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"The defined word itself is lost in OCR ('oe' for 'age'), though 'age nearest birthday' is a standard actuarial term.","reasoning_cat2":"It supports the life income options which are 'based on the payee's sex and age' (c037); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.05},
 {"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"A parenthetical note that other ages are available on request; the promise to 'furnish the amount' is administrative, not operative.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates the Option 5 note (c012) and fits the Alternate Life Income clause (c045).","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},

 {"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"Standard risk-class footnote; the 'no one is authorized to make any representation' language is clear even in garbled form.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c007, c008 and the guaranteed maximum renewal premium table it annotates.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.08},
 {"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"The definition is cut off mid-sentence so how contract months and years are measured cannot be read off the text.","reasoning_cat2":"Contract dating drives the Grace Period (c023), Renewal (c024), Incontestability (c033) and Suicide (c034) periods, so a defect here would propagate.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.16},
 {"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"'Written form acceptable to us' is a discretionary standard, and 'takes effect when signed' but 'subject to any payment made or action taken by us before we receive it' is internally awkward.","reasoning_cat2":"It governs the notices required elsewhere (conversion notice c052, ownership/beneficiary changes c026-c028), where the effective-on-signature rule could clash with those provisions' own timing.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.18},
